wa_north_ridge_3.notes: Gains the North Ridge Notch via loose, runout terrain protected by only one or two marginal small cams (narrow-head-width pieces help); published descriptions and trip reports agree this is the technical and psychological crux of the climb, with a fall here carrying serious consequences.
An unprotected slab traverse just above the notch that trip reports nickname the 'spicy' pitch — thin smearing with little gear between placements.
Enters a long simul-climbing block on mostly 4th-class terrain broken by short low-fifth-class steps on clean white granite; many parties switch to approach shoes here.
Continues up the ridge on 2nd/3rd-class ramps and corners, favoring the east (left) side of the crest for the easiest line.
More low-angle ridge scrambling on solid granite; route-finding is straightforward following the obvious crest toward the final gendarme.
A short 5.0 downclimb off a gendarme, then a traverse across the flat section of the ridge before the final summit headwall.
Starts the summit headwall: a sustained pitch up featured rock, trending right along a system of ledges (can be linked with pitch 8 on a 70m rope).
Finishes the headwall on easy 5.4 ledges to the true summit; the bolted rappel anchor here marks the top of the climb and the start of the West Ridge descent.

wa_cathedral_rock_northeast_buttress.notes: From the talus traverse under the east face, ascend the snowfield to ledges at the base of the buttress. Axe recommended early season.
From the ledges, traverse rightward toward the buttress crest on fourth-class ground.
Simul-climb the ledge system to a tree belay. This is where the route gains ground quickly.
The crux pitch: a bolt (also usable to bail), a finger crack with questionable protection, balancy moves, and a real rockfall hazard.
Above the crux the rock eases; moderate pitches up the buttress.
A third-class gully leading to the final short pitch.
A short pitch to the summit.
